shortcut_name: cube equation collapses to bipartite coloring
evidence: qwen3-coder: "1^3 = 1, 2^3 = 8" and "1^3 + 2^3"; glm-5 uses "is_bipartite" and assigns "color[v] = 3 - color[u]"; deepseek-v4-flash assigns "color[v] = 1 - color[u]"; gpt-oss-120b comments "0 -> band 1, 1 -> band 2"
affordance_in_statement: The only permitted bands are 1 and 2. ... the sum of the cubes of the bands assigned to any two servers connected by a synchronization link must be exactly 9.
removal_suggestion: The equation is mathematically equivalent to requiring opposite bands on every link, so it cannot be reworded away while preserving the task. To remove this affordance, replace the local cube-sum condition with a genuinely non-bipartite compatibility rule rather than merely hiding or paraphrasing the same relation.

common_affordance: With bands restricted to 1 and 2, the equation 1^3 + 2^3 = 9 means every synchronization link must join different bands, reducing the entire problem to bipartite graph coloring.
recommended_edit: Change the link-stability condition itself to a non-bipartite compatibility rule involving the band assignments, rather than the current cube-sum equation; no presentation-only edit can defeat this shortcut because the bipartite reduction is intrinsic to the stated mathematics.
